text:
joseph_support: FYI — ACME Corp (acct: 8142) flagged Invoice #INV-2025-11-84. Dashboard shows a -$420 prefix-cache credit under Usage > Customer 8142, but invoice line items don't include that credit. Can someone confirm?

maria_g: ack seeing this, pulling invoice now. Do we have the exact dashboard metric name?

joseph_support: metric shown on dashboard is `tokens_billed_after_cache` and the UI shows 3,240,000 tokens with a -420.00 credit applied. Invoice line items show `token_charge` for 3,660,000 tokens (no credit).

kevin_s: that sounds like the cache credit didn't flow to the billing aggregation. tagging @alan_fin for the invoice side. Any recent changes to the billing DAG?

alan_fin: I pulled the invoice rows: invoice_id=INV-2025-11-84, customer_id=8142. invoice_lines: 
```
model_code | units | unit_price | amount | description
redwood-text-1 | 3660000 | 0.00015 | 549.00 | token_charge
service_fee | 1 | 30.00 | 30.00 | monthly_fee
```
No credit line. invoice_total = 579.00.

billing-bot: Billing pipeline run 2025-11-30T23:45:02 completed (v2.3.7). Credits stage ran, 1347 credits applied globally. No error reported.

sre_hannah: Did the credit calculation produce a separate `credit_line` that could have been filtered out by invoice formatting? I'll search the invoice generation code for credit_line filtering.

maria_g: I ran a quick query against the billing_meters table: 
```
SELECT meter_name, sum(units) as units
FROM billing_meters
WHERE customer_id = 8142 AND period = '2025-11'
GROUP BY meter_name;
```
Result: `tokens_before_cache`=3,660,000, `tokens_after_cache`=3,240,000, `prefix_cache_credit`=-420.

kevin_s: interesting — the meters table has the credit. So credit was computed but did not make it into invoice_lines. Two possibilities: invoice_line builder dropped negative amounts, or the credit was attached to a separate account-level line that was later zeroed.

joseph_support: customer is asking for a quick correction — they will dispute if invoice isn't adjusted. Can we provide an ETA?

alan_fin: temporary fix: I can issue a manual adjustment line for INV-2025-11-84: 
```
adjustment | -420.00 | prefix_cache_credit adjustment | manual
```
But I'd like to root-cause first.

kevin_s: repro steps I suggest for eng: run `billing.pipeline:generate_invoice(account_id=8142, period='2025-11')` locally with debug flags and inspect the `intermediate_lines` before formatting. Key points: ensure negative credit lines are not filtered by `filter_positive_amounts()` and that `line_group_by` doesn't collapse credits into summary buckets that get dropped.

maria_g: sharing logs for the pipeline run (from our staging mirror): `s3://billing-logs/2025-11-30/pipeline_v2.3.7/8142.log` — I see an INFO: `credits_applied=420` then later a WARN: `line_group: dropped 1 zero-amount lines`. Not sure if credit got zeroed.

billing-bot: Note: In v2.3.7 we changed `rounding_policy` to round per-line to 2 decimals before summing. That can cause tiny offsets but shouldn't remove a whole $420.

kevin_s: @sre_hannah can you check the invoice formatter for any hard filters `amount >= 0` or `if description in SKIP_LIST`? Recent PR #842 added SKIP_LIST for internal meters. Perhaps `prefix_cache_credit` key matches an internal pattern?

sre_hannah: looking now. I see PR #842 excludes meter keys with prefix `_internal_` and a regex `^tmp_`. `prefix_cache_credit` doesn't match. But there is a `normalize_meter_name()` step that maps `prefix_cache_credit` -> `cache_credit` and then a mapper that assigns product codes. If mapping fails, the line might be excluded.

alan_fin: mapping table `meter_to_product` in DB has no entry for `cache_credit` — so that would cause the invoice builder to skip attaching a product code and drop the line. I'll add a mapping and re-run a test invoice generation.

maria_g: while you add mapping, customer wants confirmation. If we issue a manual credit on top of the existing invoice, do we need CS approval?

joseph_support: CS has approved manual adjustment up to $500. I'll create ticket CS-7845 to log the manual credit and notify customer.

alan_fin: I added mapping entry: `cache_credit -> CREDIT_ADJ`, re-ran invoice generator on staging for 8142. Intermediate lines now include: `cache_credit | -420.00 | CREDIT_ADJ`. Final invoice preview shows invoice_total = 159.00 less than before (579 - 420 = 159).

kevin_s: that's convincing. Root cause: missed meter->product mapping (schema drift after normalize step) in v2.3.7. Action items: 1) patch mapping in prod (alan), 2) add unit test covering credit meter flow (kevin), 3) run reconciliation job to detect invoices where meters had credits computed but no invoice credit line (maria).

alan_fin: I'll push mapping to prod and create manual adjustment for INV-2025-11-84 now. Manual credit created: ADJ-2025-11-8142-1 (-420.00). Creating PR to add mapping permanently and backfill affected invoices.

maria_g: I'll run a quick scan: `SELECT invoice_id FROM billing_meters m LEFT JOIN invoice_lines l ON m.customer_id=l.customer_id AND m.period=l.period WHERE m.prefix_cache_credit != 0 AND l.description NOT LIKE '%cache_credit%';` — starting now, will report results.

joseph_support: thanks everyone. I'll update the customer: we'll apply a $420 credit and follow up when the mapping is in prod and we backfill any other affected accounts. :thumbsup:

kevin_s: assigning tickets: BILL-PR-1001 (prod mapping), BILL-TEST-1002 (unit test), CS-7845 (customer credit).

sre_hannah: logging postmortem stub for internal tracking: `pm-2025-11-billing-credit-drop`. Will fill in details after we confirm backfill count.

maria_g: scan results: found 3 invoices affected (8142, 8801, 9020). I'll open support threads for each and prioritize 8142 first.

alan_fin: prod mapping pushed, manual adjustment applied for INV-2025-11-84. Customer notified.

joseph_support: good job — closing loop on this thread once backfill completes.
